top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Paris-Roubaix Challenge. Practice on cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 106 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Paris-Roubaix Challenge's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
At mile 60 of 106, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Paris-Roubaix Challenge. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
When someone attacks on cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Paris-Roubaix Challenge's cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Smooth pedaling at 106 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Paris-Roubaix Challenge. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,600ft of climbing on cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads does to your power file on race day.
At Paris-Roubaix Challenge, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
106 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.weather: April in Busigny to Roubaix Velodrome, Nord, France — Mid-April in northern France is raw. Temperatures range from 5-15C (41-59F), with rain a strong probability. Wet cobblestones transform from difficult to treacherous — grip drops dramatically, mud fills the gaps between stones, and spray from other riders reduces visibility. The wind across the flat agricultural plains of northern France is relentless and often strong. This is not a sun-drenched Mediterranean sportive. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Paris-Roubaix Challenge. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Paris-Roubaix Challenge’s 106 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Paris-Roubaix Challenge demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 106 miles of cobblestoned sectors (pave) and paved roads in Busigny to Roubaix Velodrome, Nord, France.
